4.stem: The student wants to describe, for a technically minded reader, precisely how the researchers measured the glacier's retreat. Which choice best accomplishes this goal?

options.A: The glacier feeds a river used for irrigation downstream, which is why the researchers wanted a precise record of how far its front edge moved from one summer to the next.
options.B: Warmer summers accelerated the retreat, with the terminus giving way fastest in the years when the melt season began earliest.
options.C: The researchers compared satellite images taken each summer from 2000 to 2020, measuring the horizontal distance the terminus moved between successive images.
options.D: The glacier's terminus retreated an average of 30 meters a year over the two decades studied, a figure reported for the period as a whole rather than for any one summer.

5.stem: The student wants to emphasize the contrast between the old explanation for ulcers and the newer one. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: The bacterium responsible for most peptic ulcers was identified in 1982 by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren, who then proved that it caused them.
options.B: Doctors once blamed ulcers on stress and spicy food, but Marshall and Warren showed that the bacterium H. pylori causes most of them.
options.C: To demonstrate what the bacterium actually does inside a human stomach, Marshall famously drank a culture of H. pylori that he had prepared.
options.D: Marshall and Warren's identification of the bacterium behind most peptic ulcers was recognized with a Nobel Prize more than two decades later.

6.stem: The student wants to make a generalization about the link between tree canopy and temperature that a skeptical reader would find well supported. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: City B's tree canopy grew from 15 percent in 2015 to 25 percent in 2020, a rise of 10 points in five years.
options.B: In City A tree canopy rose from 12 percent in 2015 to 20 percent in 2020, and over those same five years the average summer temperature fell from 34°C to 32°C.
options.C: A 2021 review of 40 cities found that each 10-point rise in tree canopy corresponded to about 1.2°C of cooling, indicating the pattern holds broadly.
options.D: Between 2015 and 2020 both City A and City B increased their tree canopy and recorded lower average summer temperatures.

9.stem: The student wants to emphasize the practical application of the research. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Vidal's beacon is ready for working harbors: because a charged unit stays lit for fifteen days without sun and kept flashing through sub-freezing temperatures, crews could service each buoy once every two years instead of every six months.
options.B: Vidal's beacon is ready for working harbors: because a charged unit stays lit for eighteen days without sun and kept flashing through storm-driven waves, crews could service each buoy once every three years instead of every six months.
options.C: Vidal's beacon is ready for working harbors: because a charged unit stays lit for nine days without sun and kept flashing through heavy snowfall, crews could service each buoy once every four years instead of every six months.
options.D: Vidal's beacon is ready for working harbors: because a charged unit stays lit for twelve days without sun and kept flashing through dense fog, crews could service each buoy once every five years instead of every six months.

12.stem: The student wants to acknowledge a limitation of the study. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Anand's result is limited in scope, however: because every plot grew the single cultivar 'Nevada' and relative humidity was held at one fixed level, the 50 percent optimum may not hold for other cultivars or at other humidity levels.
options.B: Anand's result is limited in scope, however: because every plot grew the single cultivar 'Salinas' and daytime air temperature was held at one fixed level, the 50 percent optimum may not hold for other cultivars or at other temperatures.
options.C: Anand's result is limited in scope, however: because every plot grew the single cultivar 'Parris Island' and carbon dioxide concentration was held at one fixed level, the 50 percent optimum may not hold for other cultivars or at other carbon dioxide levels.
options.D: Anand's result is limited in scope, however: because every plot grew the single cultivar 'Concept' and irrigation volume was held at one fixed level, the 50 percent optimum may not hold for other cultivars or at other irrigation rates.

14.stem: The student wants to use the dolphin-and-shark example to illustrate the general principle of convergent evolution. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Dolphins are mammals, whereas sharks are fish.
options.B: Convergent evolution occurs when unrelated species independently evolve similar traits.
options.C: Dolphins and sharks illustrate convergent evolution: though separated by over 400 million years, both independently evolved streamlined bodies suited to fast swimming.
options.D: Both dolphins and sharks adapted their shapes for fast swimming in open water.

15.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in migration distance between the two butterfly species. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: While the monarch migrates up to 3,000 miles annually, the painted lady travels as far as 9,000 miles.
options.B: Each year the monarch travels from Canada to central Mexico, a journey of up to 3,000 miles.
options.C: The painted lady migrates between Europe and sub-Saharan Africa, covering as much as 9,000 miles.
options.D: Both the monarch and the painted lady are counted among the insects that migrate the longest distances.

16.stem: The student wants to emphasize the lake's recovery after decades of pollution. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: After pollution closed the lake to swimmers in 1980, a cleanup restored it and swimmers returned in 2018.
options.B: A cleanup effort began at the lake in 2005.
options.C: Pollution forced the lake to close to swimmers by 1980.
options.D: In the 1950s, the lake was a popular spot for swimming.

18.stem: The writer wants to emphasize the causal chain linking sea otters to the health of kelp forests. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: In the stretches of coast where sea otters had been hunted out by fur traders — populations of sea urchins exploded across the seafloor within only a few seasons of the otters' disappearance.
options.B: Kelp forests returned to health in exactly those stretches of coast where sea otters were eventually reestablished after the hunting stopped.
options.C: By eating urchins that graze kelp, otters hold urchin numbers down and let kelp thrive, so kelp collapsed when otters were hunted out and rebounded when they returned.
options.D: Sea urchins graze on kelp, the tall algae whose dense underwater stands make up the kelp forests found along these coasts.

19.stem: The student wants to counter a reader's assumption that the Welsh language is dying out. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Far from vanishing, Welsh had rebounded to about 540,000 speakers by 2021, with notable gains among children under 15.
options.B: Welsh was spoken by about 500,000 people in 1991, a decade before the count that recorded a further decline.
options.C: Welsh-medium schools expanded in the years after 2001, following a decade in which the number of Welsh speakers had fallen by some 20,000.
options.D: Welsh speaker numbers fell from about 500,000 in 1991 to about 480,000 in 2001, a loss of roughly 20,000 speakers in a single decade.

20.stem: The student wants to emphasize the study's main finding. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: The survey's central result is clear: barnacles dominated the growth by weight in every zone, and the fouling layer averaged 14 millimeters thick.
options.B: The survey's central result is clear: tube worms dominated the growth by weight in every zone, and the fouling layer averaged 24 millimeters thick.
options.C: The survey's central result is clear: blue mussels dominated the growth by weight in every zone, and the fouling layer averaged 19 millimeters thick.
options.D: The survey's central result is clear: sea squirts dominated the growth by weight in every zone, and the fouling layer averaged 29 millimeters thick.

21.stem: The student wants to present a cautious summary of the findings. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Over the 10-week trial, evening use of the path rose by 23 percent, though Brathwaite cautions that the trial ran entirely in autumn, when daylight hours were shrinking week by week, so the increase cannot yet be credited to the lighting.
options.B: Over the 6-week trial, evening use of the path rose by 14 percent, though Brathwaite cautions that the trial covered only one 400-meter stretch, with no unlit path used for comparison, so the increase cannot yet be credited to the lighting.
options.C: Over the 12-week trial, evening use of the path rose by 28 percent, though Brathwaite cautions that the pre-trial baseline came from a one-day manual tally rather than continuous logging, so the increase cannot yet be credited to the lighting.
options.D: Over the 8-week trial, evening use of the path rose by 19 percent, though Brathwaite cautions that the counts came from a single sensor that could not separate walkers from cyclists, so the increase cannot yet be credited to the lighting.

22.stem: The student wants to emphasize the causal chain linking the wolves to the recovery of the riverside trees. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: After wolves returned in 1995, elk avoided the open valleys, allowing the willow and aspen along the rivers to regrow.
options.B: Wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone National Park in 1995.
options.C: Songbird numbers rose following the wolves' return.
options.D: Beaver colonies increased from one to twelve after the reintroduction.

23.stem: The student wants to emphasize that a single factor was behind several of the observed changes. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Rising ocean temperatures drove several changes at once—bleaching corals, shifting fish ranges northward, and intensifying tropical storms.
options.B: Tropical storms grew more intense in 2016, the same year in which coral bleaching sharply reduced the revenue that the region earned from tourism.
options.C: Fishers reported changes in the species they caught after warming waters shifted fish ranges northward during 2016.
options.D: Coral bleaching in 2016 reduced revenue from tourism, and in that same year fishers along the coast reported changes in the species they caught.
